observations: Photo 0 shows a yellow industrial diesel engine block with fuel filter, pulley, wiring harness and various fittings; paint color consistent with Caterpillar machinery but no legible brand/model text visible.

Photo 1 shows a close-up of the valve cover assembly with a metal nameplate attached; the plate has embossed/printed characters but they are too blurred and small to read reliably (appears to show partial letters/numbers, not clearly 'C9').
Engine appears largely intact (fuel filter housing, injectors, valve cover, pulley system still attached) rather than stripped into loose parts.
No overall engine serial plate, data tag, or full engine shot showing mounting points, flywheel housing, or injection pump is visible.
No video or sound/start-up evidence; no shot showing internal condition (pistons, bores, crankshaft) despite seller labeling it 'parts'.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows a nameplate but the text is not legible enough to confirm 'C9' or even 'Caterpillar' branding; yellow paint is suggestive but not proof.
No internal shots, compression test, or start-up video provided to confirm running condition either way.
Photos show an intact-looking assembly but no full side/front/rear views to confirm turbo, injectors, ECU, flywheel, and accessories are all present.

risks.risk: Model cannot be confirmed as C9 vs another Caterpillar family (e.g., 3208, C11, C7), which drives a large price swing.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine ID/data plate showing model and serial number.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced against any specific Caterpillar model comparable; treated as unidentified diesel engine of unknown model

risks.risk: Internal condition unknown; 'parts' label may mean cracked block, seized internals, or missing internals not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video of engine being turned over or compression test readout, plus photos of oil pan drain and cylinder bores if disassembled.

risks.risk: Completeness unclear: turbocharger, injection pump, ECU, wiring loom, flywheel housing not all shown.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree walk-around photos/video showing all sides including rear bellhousing and front accessory drive.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming missing major accessories unless shown

risks.risk: Possible water/corrosion damage or external cracks not visible due to dirt and poor lighting.
risks.proof: Close, well-lit photos of block casting, water jacket areas, and any visible cracks or weld repairs.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having unknown hidden damage, worst case

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit close-up of the engine data/ID plate showing full model number and serial number.
Full walk-around photos/video (all four sides, top and bottom) showing completeness of accessories (turbo, injection pump, ECU, flywheel, starter, alternator).
Video of the engine being turned/cranked, or a compression test result, to establish actual running condition.
Any paperwork (CAT parts invoice, import documents) linking this unit to a verified C9 serial range.
response.reason: The seller's key pricing claim — that this is specifically a Caterpillar C9 — cannot be read from either photo, and no comparable exists for an unidentified or wrong-model Caterpillar engine; the model that sets the price is unreadable.
